main_text.p: An non saltem occidere li-cebit in casu, quo quis fuerit ab alio provocatus? Non equi-dem. Neque enim id ipsum fie-ret ad defensionem, verùm ad vindictam Arg. l. 45. D. Ad l. Aquil. l. 2. 3. Cod. l. Corn. de Si-car. Vasq. Illustr. quæst. l. 1. c. 18. n. 15. Bocer. l. 2. de Bell. duell. n. 17. Accedit, quòd hac ratione, quivis sibi ipsi jus diceret; adeoque sibi assumeret, id quod spectat officium Magistratus: contra l. unic. Cod. Ne quis in suâ causâ. judic. l. ult. Cod. de Vi Privat. l. 14. Cod. de Judæis & cœlic. l. 176. D. de Reg. jur.

Verùm an non censebitur provocatus infamiam aliquam incurrere, si non comparuerit, praesertim si nobilis fuerit, aut miles? Minimè gentium. Qui enim legis dicto est obediens, nec juris, nec facti infamiâ no-tatur.

page.notes: The running head reads "De Duellis." and the page number is 377 at top right. The gathering signature "R" stands at the foot, between the words "no-" and "tatur." on the last line. The text of the last line is "notatur." Possible doubt: "vindictam" (the ct ligature is hard to read on the scan) and "cœlic." are read from the print but not fully certain.
